items.title: BlockStrap: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Template Engine Injection
items.summary: This critical vulnerability, dubbed 'BlockStrap', allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution by injecting malicious PHP code into the template engine. Adobe released a fix on October 13, 2026, though Sansec warns of its high exploitability despite Adobe's Priority 2 rating.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization leading to Unauthenticated Code Execution in B2B
items.summary: Part of the APSB26-153 bulletin, this critical flaw in Adobe Commerce B2B allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code due to incorrect authorization.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization (Privilege Escalation / Security Feature Bypass)
items.summary: This high-severity vulnerability allows a low-privileged, authenticated attacker to bypass security controls and gain unauthorized read and write access to protected resources. It was disclosed as part of APSB26-153.

items.title: StyleSmuggler: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE)
items.summary: This zero-day vulnerability, actively exploited in the wild, allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution by injecting malicious code into Magento's template system. Adobe released an emergency hotfix on September 7, 2026, with a CVSS score of 10.0.

items.title: Multiple Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerabilities
items.summary: This bulletin addresses multiple critical stored XSS flaws, two of which are exploitable without authentication, potentially leading to security feature bypass and privilege escalation.

items.title: Multiple Incorrect Authorization Vulnerabilities
items.summary: APSB26-138 includes several critical incorrect authorization flaws, with six of the eight vulnerabilities in the bulletin exploitable without authentication, potentially leading to security feature bypass and privilege escalation.

items.title: PolyShell: Unrestricted File Upload leading to Remote Code Execution
items.summary: This critical vulnerability, known as PolyShell, allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload a file with a dangerous type, which the server then treats as code, leading to arbitrary code execution. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27, 2026, due to active exploitation.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization (Privilege Escalation)
items.summary: This critical incorrect authorization flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to elevate their privileges, potentially taking over other customer accounts. Exploitation attempts were observed shortly after Adobe released patches on August 11, 2026.

items.title: Multiple Cross-site Scripting (Stored XSS) Vulnerabilities
items.summary: APSB26-92 addresses multiple high-severity stored XSS vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
